newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Pioneer for Polifarbs merger, but amended.
newsitem.headline: Polish Pioneer for Polifarbs merger, but amended.

text.p: The Pioneer First Polish Trust Fund Co, which has stakes in Polifarb Cieszyn and Wroclaw, is for the firms' planned merger but would like to change the way it is done, Pioneer's president said.

Alicja Malecka told Reuters on Friday that Pioneer, owned by Boston-based Pioneer Group, would like Polifarb Cieszyn's shareholders to get 53.5 percent of the future merged firm and current Wroclaw shareholders 46.5 percent.
"According to our analyses Polifarb Cieszyn is worth more than Wroclaw -- 1.3 to one according to purely mathematical calculations and 1.15 to one if we take into account other factors," she said.
She added other factors included the firms' potential development before the merger.
Malecka said Pioneer would like Cieszyn's planned bonus issue before the firms merge to be greater than the 2,978,820 shares proposed by Cieszyn, but did not give precise figures.
Pioneer has about 10 percent of shares in Polifarb Cieszyn and 1.5 percent in Polifarb Wroclaw.

Cieszyn has said it would carry out the bonus issue to equal Wroclaw's 22,103,820 shares and later set another issue of 22,103,820 shares for Wroclaw shareholders to facilitate a one-for-one share exchange to effect the merger.
The Polifarbs plan a one-for-five rights issue of up to 8.2 million shares after the merger to expand their distribution network, sales and marketing, and invest in other paintmakers.
Polifarb Cieszyn's shareholders will vote on the merger on March 24, Polifarb Wroclaw's on March 25.
The new entity, Polifarb Cieszyn-Wroclaw SA, is expected to produce about 40 percent of domestic-made paint and command a 26-percent market share.
